correctness.rationale: For payoffs with 0<c<v, best response is contribution exactly when all neighbors abstain. New-edge equilibria are partitioned into old valid profiles minus those with both endpoints selected (c[d]c[n-d]), plus profiles in which one previously undominated chord endpoint is rescued by the selected opposite endpoint (2c[d-2]c[n-d-2]). The exact composition bijections include short-arc boundary values. The double Padovan recurrence D(d,m) with bases D(d,3)=0, D(d,2) at d=2,3,4 equals (1,0,2), and D(d,4) equals (2,0,3) proves strict uniqueness away from d=3 or m=3. The difference sequence c[j]-c[j-1] proves the distance-two paradox. Dominant-root analysis proves the asymptotic. Independently re-enumerated every profile n=5..17 and verified 21353 assertions from check.py; tests are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: A well-defined exact equilibrium-multiplicity optimization on one-chord rings was not implied by the checked pure-equilibrium characterization or the original unchorded-cycle count. The loss/rescue formula and all-chord strict optimum are the new claims. The inspected full texts of the model and cycle-count papers discuss distinct graph interventions/objects. Published extremal graph-class bounds and OEIS Perrin entries do not determine the chord-specific equilibrium multiplicity. Historical priority remains provisional under the listed risk.
residual_risks: The exact same formula might exist in an unindexed paper or table under an alternative term such as bicyclic-graph maximal independence polynomial or independent domination polynomial.

value.rationale: The game-theoretic object is natural: binary local public-good provision has many equilibria and a planner may want to understand how a single new link affects coordination multiplicity. The exact one-link classification, strict optimal chord distance, and paradoxical increase under a shorter chord are structural results with an all-size mathematical mechanism, not one-off small-graph counts. The sharp asymptotic relative reduction (~17.7 percent) quantifies the optimization. Value is confined to equilibrium multiplicity, not utility or empirical predictions.
